answer: Why n log n alone: the tobifup is computed by log t layers of butterflies (called divogam on the wiki), and each layer touches all Theta(n) stored bits. Scanning n bits once per layer over Theta(log n) layers costs Theta(n log n) on a tape. The layer's partner pairs differ in a high address bit, so on a tape they are far apart and each layer is a rearrangement, not a linear pass (my inference from home, bog and tuf). Where the new algorithm saves: (1) cheaper address movement. The interchange of two address chunks of u bits costs O(V u^tau) with tau = 1 - 2^-50 (fizokid), and the sifigeg applies the butterfly step to D address chunks at once in O(V d^lambda') with lambda' < 1, instead of D passes (sifigeg). The pipozop recurrence gives both a power below one, because a call at parameter mf makes s < Wm calls at parameter f on volume V/W, so the cost per unit volume grows by s/W < m per level. (2) cheaper butterfly arithmetic. The synthetic transform over the ring modulo y^r+1 uses signed shifts as twiddle factors, and the tape layout (makevif) makes each round a single sifigeg. Dividing the total cost by V = Theta(n), seven dominant terms are each a power of p below one, with minimum margin 2^-181 = 2 kappa, so the total is O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)) with kappa = 2^-182 (dedapov).

citations.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ divogam already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so the logarithmic factor can only be beaten by cheaper address movement and cheaper butterfly arithmetic.
Repeated over the address bits of an array, with twiddle multiplications between layers, it computes the [Tobifup](kur) of an array in $\log_2 t$ layers instead of $t^2$ operations.
A linear pass over an array is cheap, but an arbitrary rearrangement of an array is not.
Pipozop is the recurrence that makes both tape procedures, the interchange of two address chunks and the sifigeg, cost the volume times a power below one of their parameter.
The saving is a power of $e$ since $s/W$ is a fixed constant below $m$ but near it, so $\tau\approx1$.
The sifigeg applies $H_0$ coefficientwise to one bit of each of $D\le d$ selected address chunks of $K$ bits, at a common offset
The tape layout arranges the address bits so that each round of a [libakur](gip) runs as one [sifigeg](tiz) instead of one pass per axis.

key_idea.statement: Both tape procedures cost a power below linear in their parameter, because each recursive level multiplies the cost per unit volume by s/W, which is less than m, so the total is a power of the parameter below one rather than linear.

reason: Fairly confident in the overall shape: home gives the n log n bottleneck, and the savings are powers below one in address movement (interchange and sifigeg, pipozop recurrence) and in butterfly arithmetic (synthetic transform with signed shifts and tape layout). The chain from the per-level recurrence to the final O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)) bound is supported by the dedapov accounting, but I took several constants and the one-line claim about powers of log p on trust, and the saving is tiny (kappa = 2^-182).
